content: 1. The overgrowth of organisms that are not susceptible to the medication, including fungi, may occur. If a superinfection develops, appropriate therapy should be initiated promptly. 2. Pregnancy Category B: This medication should be used during pregnancy only if the potential benefits outweigh the potential risks to the fetus. 3. Lactation: Use this medication with caution during breastfeeding, as there is no available data on its safety in lactating individuals. 4. Category A: This category indicates that the medication is generally considered acceptable, as controlled studies in pregnant women have not demonstrated any evidence of fetal risk. 5. The medication has a half-life of 3 to 6 hours in individuals with normal renal function. 6. Metabolism: Not applicable (N/A). 7. Excretion: Approximately 60% of the medication is excreted in the urine, with less than 1% excreted as the unchanged drug. 8. Dialyzability: The medication is not removed by hemodialysis (HD) or peritoneal dialysis (PD). 9. Mechanism of action: The medication is bactericidal, causing leakage of the bacterial membrane by binding to phospholipids. 10. Additive interactions: The medication may have additive effects when combined with amphotericin B, chloramphenicol sodium succinate, chlorothiazide, heparin, magnesium sulfate (MgSO4), and other specified agents. 11. Syringe compatibility: The medication may be compatible with ampicillin (uncertain). 12. Additive compatibility: The medication is compatible with amikacin, ascorbic acid, colistimethate, diphenhydramine, erythromycin lactobionate, hydrocortisone sodium succinate, kanamycin, penicillin G potassium, penicillin G sodium, phenobarbital, ranitidine, and vitamins B and C. 13. Syringe compatibility: The medication is compatible with penicillin G sodium. 14. Y-site compatibility: The medication is compatible with esmolol. 15. Intravenous (IV) administration: Dilute 500,000 units of the medication in 300-500 mL of D5W (5% dextrose in water) and infuse over 60-90 minutes. 16. Intramuscular (IM) administration: Reconstitute the vial with 2 mL of sterile water for injection (SWI), normal saline (NS), or a 1% procaine hydrochloride solution. Administer deeply into the upper outer quadrant of the gluteal muscles. 17. Intrathecal (IT) administration: Reconstitute the vial with 10 mL of normal saline (NS). Do not use procaine hydrochloride for intrathecal administration. 18. Proper disposal: Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Discard this product properly when it is expired or no longer needed. 19. Overdose: In the event of an overdose with serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. 20. Important information: This document provides a summary and does not contain all possible information about the product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. 21.
